beats.text: One brooch is carved from a meteorite strike.
beats.note: The scarab at its centre is cut from natural yellow-green glass scattered across the Sahara. Ancient Egyptian jewellers were carving genuine impact glass, not shaping paint or dye.

beats.context: How long before Tutankhamun's reign a rock-shattering impact melted Saharan sand into the glass his jeweller later carved.

beats.lead: For decades, nobody could prove how
beats.text: It might have been an explosion in the air, not on the ground.
beats.note: A 100-megaton airburst, 200 times the 2013 Chelyabinsk event, could melt sand without leaving a crater. The debate ran for years.

beats.lead: The proof turned up inside the glass itself
beats.text: A mineral that only forms from a real ground impact.
beats.note: Reidite, found in roughly one in ten zircon grains across every sample tested, needs shock pressure an airburst cannot produce.

beats.text: No crater has been found. The glass proves the strike happened anyway.

beats.line: A pharaoh wore evidence of an impact, three thousand years before anyone could read it.
